review: Bounded security closure of known extraction findings

snapshot.verification: Manifest SHA-256, each listed file length, and each listed file SHA-256 were independently checked against artifacts/extraction-review-03/files/.

scope: Bounded closure of the four findings in artifacts/extraction-security/closure.json plus explicitly assigned follow-up fixes. No broad P2 hunt. No source, MC, Chrome profile, registry, live download, or snapshot was modified or accessed. No tests or helper binaries were run by this reviewer.

findings.summary: Admission now serializes cross-process worker counting and queued-state creation, caps live jobs at four, and rejects capacity before creating a new job record or spawning a worker.

evidence.detail: MAX_WORKERS is 4 and queue lock wait is bounded at 2 hours.
dispatch.lock protects active-worker counting; capacity failure returns before job state is written or a worker is spawned.
Existing IDs are handled before secret retrieval and new-job admission; identity/fingerprint mismatch returns job-conflict, while a matching saved result is replayed.
worker-capacity is treated as a retryable reply for the same pending ID.
The helper's queued work and queue wait behavior are documented.

verification.tests: Parent reports 22 final Rust tests and final package acceptance pass in artifacts/extraction-native/rar-acceptance.json. I read the frozen report; I did not execute these tests.
verification.remaining: Malformed job records conservatively consume capacity; this can reduce availability but does not provide a cap bypass. No P0/P1 gap found in this bounded finding.

findings.summary: Queue wait and each engine child operation now have finite deadlines; Windows timeout cleanup kills the Job Object and reaps the child. Worker breakaway retries without breakaway only on AccessDenied.

evidence.detail: Per-child operation timeout is 30 minutes; queue wait timeout is 2 hours.
Windows child processes use kill-on-close Job Object handling and deadline wait/termination/reap paths for test, extraction, and listing.
Listing output collection is bounded and its child is still polled against the deadline.
Breakaway fallback is limited to Windows ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED; other spawn errors are returned.
A Windows unit case exercises an actual short child timeout and checks termination/reaping.

verification.reviewerStaticReview: verified source paths and control flow in frozen snapshot
verification.tests: Parent reports native 22/22, including actual Windows timeout coverage, in artifacts/extraction-native/rar-acceptance.json. I read that report and did not rerun it.
verification.remaining: The 30-minute deadline applies per subprocess, so multiple sequential operations can take longer in total; this is finite and matches the assigned fix. Breakaway fallback can inherit the caller's job lifetime; README documents this limitation.

findings.summary: Indefinite logical validity is closed: secret blobs expire after seven days, future mtimes are treated as expired, and expired secrets are rejected and removed on use. Cleanup is intentionally lazy, so seven days is not a guaranteed physical-deletion deadline while the helper is unused.

evidence.detail: Secret TTL is seven days and a cleanup pass inspects at most 128 candidates.
Age at or beyond TTL and future modification times are expired; non-regular or reparse files are rejected.
Cleanup enumerates/sorts valid secret names, advances a persistent cursor, and inspects at most 128 candidates per pass for fair progress.
Read rejects and removes an expired secret; the blob read is size bounded.
Cleanup runs on StoreSecret and Status; Ping also invokes cleanup. There is no background timer.
Documentation states failed-group retry retention, seven-day expiry, future-mtime handling, 128-item pass/cursor behavior, lazy request-driven cleanup, and residual encrypted data on uninstall.
Pending secret deletion IDs are durable and retried with backoff when helper deletion is unavailable.

verification.reviewerStaticReview: verified expiry, delete-on-read, cleanup triggers, and documentation against frozen source
verification.tests: Parent reports 114 TypeScript tests and 22 Rust tests pass; I read snapshot verification and source/test definitions but did not run tests.
verification.residualCounterevidence: If the helper receives no later Ping, StoreSecret, Status, or secret read, an expired ciphertext file may remain on disk beyond seven days. The TTL bounds helper-mediated use, not wall-clock physical erasure; DPAPI remains at-rest protection rather than same-user isolation. This is disclosed, not represented as guaranteed deletion.

findings.summary: Installer now snapshots owned manifest/config and prior registration, stages replacement files, commits registration last, and rolls back files and registration on caught failures. Incomplete rollback retains backups and reports their location.

evidence.detail: Ownership and existing manifest/config content are validated before replacement.
Prior files and registration are backed up; staged writes and registration commit are transactional with rollback and backup retention on incomplete rollback.
Fault injection uses a fixture and mock registry state, not the real registry.

verification.tests: Snapshot manifest reports installer rollback pass with mocked registry. Parent specifically reports it was run without real registry; I did not run it.
verification.remaining: Abrupt process termination or power loss cannot run the catch-based rollback; preserved backup files require recovery. No issue remains for ordinary caught failures.

evidence.detail: Request/job path keys are normalized consistently, including UNC forms; replay validates secret ID and path/source fingerprints before returning a saved result.
Existing matching jobs return before reading an expired/forgotten secret, preserving idempotent retries without weakening identity checks.

followUpFixes.verification: Reviewer confirmed source control flow. Parent reports focused TypeScript/browser acceptance; no independent runtime execution by this reviewer.

evidence.detail: Atomic write removes temporary files after post-create write/sync/replace failures.
Initial extracting-state persistence failure is recorded as failed while the worker still owns the job lock, before engine execution continues.
Terminal commit takes the job lock with blocking wait, avoiding a dropped terminal result on transient lock contention.
Deterministic cross-process lock-holder test covers blocking terminal commit.
Fault injection covers temporary-file cleanup and subsequent retry after write/sync/replace failures.

followUpFixes.verification: Reviewer inspected source and test definitions. Parent reports final 22 Rust tests pass; did not rerun.

evidence.detail: RAR volume parser accepts positive numeric part suffixes including part1/part01 and does not reject an ordinary filename merely for containing '.part'.
Archive listing rejects only non-empty Symbolic Link/Hard Link targets.
Unit test permits empty RAR5 link metadata while rejecting non-empty targets, including whitespace-padded values.

Reviewer read report and source; did not run acceptance.

evidence.detail: Frozen report status is pass; cleanup booleans for test profiles, server, registry fixture, helper worker, and isolated helper state are all true.
Runtime report and final helper SHA-256 0316baf852b8d486c9bb88c9433957dec4622f2ea1c6b69ce4d0970f77e1558c are bound into the snapshot.

followUpFixes.verification: Read and hash-verified report as a snapshot entry; this reviewer did not run Chrome E2E or inspect a personal Chrome profile.

evidence.detail: Package publishing stages outputs and attempts rollback, retaining recovery backups and reporting incomplete rollback.
Frozen package report identifies the 7-Zip 26.04 helper bundle, static CRT, 13 dependency notices, and no system install/registration.
Final helper06 bundle is the tested artifact; its hash is recorded with bundled engine identity.

followUpFixes.verification: Static files and frozen reports inspected; packaging command not rerun.

reviewProcess.codeReview: Parent reports three CodeRabbit rounds covering 33/11/4 files and seven issues fixed; the third-round hourly limit stopped another submission. This closure does not claim CodeRabbit reported zero remaining findings.
reviewerPerformed: Verified review-03 manifest SHA-256 and all 42 entry sizes and SHA-256 hashes.
Compared assigned native admission, timeout, secret expiry, idempotent replay, atomic state, RAR metadata, installer rollback, tests, and reports against frozen snapshot source.
reviewerDidNotPerform: Did not run Rust/TypeScript tests, package build, installer test, native helper, or Chrome E2E.
Did not access personal Chrome, real registry, live downloads, or system installation; no claim of general OS sandboxing or complete native security.
reviewProcess.boundedConclusion: The four carried findings are closed as described, with lazy physical secret deletion and crash/power-loss recovery explicitly retained as limitations. No P0/P1 gap was found in this bounded closure.
